content:
This is really a question for @Thomas Zhu  and @Pietro Monticone . Is LeanArchitect suited for a project like PhysLean (i.e. similar in structure or organisation to Mathlib) compared to a project which is more focused on a single target or broad goal?

(Sorry @Thomas Zhu had to subscribe you to the channel so you would get the ping here).

The purpose of LeanArchitect is to automate blueprint annotation, so our hope is that it would make sense to use LeanArchitect whenever it would make sense to use a blueprint. So the real question is probably whether PhysLean needs a blueprint. In my opinion blueprints benefit both projects focused on a single target and more open-ended projects, but that would be up to you!
Maybe LeanArchitect isn't quite the right thing for PhysLib - but I would very much like a way we could bake the requirements of APIs (see the API type issues) directly into the project.
